name: hitsville-eq-mix-glue
description: Gentle broadband 'Motown polish' for a full mix bus or a master-stage tonal tilt, from the UADx Hitsville EQ. Small dial moves keep the proportional-Q broad, so this behaves like a smooth tilt rather than surgical bells: 50 +2 (sub/weight), 320 -1 (clear the low-mids), 5000 +1 (presence), 12500 +1 (air), GAIN -1. A clean, no-distortion macro EQ (0.000% THD). For the precise stereo-linked/finer-step version on a master, prefer the 'uaudio_hitsville_eq_mastering.vst3' variant.
intended_for: a stereo mix bus or a master tonal-shaping stage where you want a musical Motown tilt with tiny moves. On a master keep every band <= +/-2 and check streaming-target loudness afterward; for surgical work use [[fabfilter-pro-q-4]].
plugin_build: UADx 'uaudio_hitsville_eq.vst3' (UADx native — RENDERS headless via Pedalboard, no-iLok). The mastering twin 'uaudio_hitsville_eq_mastering.vst3' loads the same way if you want the precision/stereo-link version.

target_signature.comment: measured dry->processed on projects/watercolors/mix/bus_warm_pre_dry.wav via the harness (peak-trim -1 dBFS). Dry: crest 23.6, centroid 3128, tilt -2.26, low 0.542, low_mid 0.378, high 0.0115. (Drum bus stands in for a mix here; on a real full mix the deltas are gentler.)

notes: Small settings on purpose: at +/-1..+2 the proportional-Q is broad (measured peak:octave ~1.1 at +2), so the curve is a smooth tilt — ideal on a full bus. Don't reach for big boosts on a mix/master.
Clean EQ, no colour (0.000% THD). GAIN -1 compensates; never GAIN-BOOST hot material (clips past 0 dBFS).
On a master, re-check with [G] check-streaming-targets after; this is a tonal stage, not a limiter.
